observation.visible_scene: A static macro close-up against a near-black background shows a fuzzy, fibrous reddish-pink mound occupying the lower-center of the frame. A small blue circular spot sits near the middle of the mound, with bluish-green fringes along the bottom left and right edges of the object. A pale yellowish/amber droplet-like feature is visible at the lower center of the mound, and a glossier darker-red bulge sits on the right side of the mound. A 'Macro Tube' watermark is fixed in the bottom-right corner throughout.
visible_changes: The object does not translate across the frame and the watermark and background edges stay aligned, indicating the camera is essentially stationary; the visible changes are local to the object's surface.
The right-side red bulge gradually becomes smoother and more dome-like/glossy over the sequence (a slow swelling or wetting of the surface rather than a movement of the whole object).
The small amber/yellowish feature at the lower center of the mound appears to grow slightly and gain a clearer droplet highlight from early to late frames.
The overall illumination/exposure shifts subtly: the mound reads more orange-pink in the earliest frames and deeper, more saturated red with stronger specular highlights in later frames.
The central blue spot and the blue-green base fringes remain in the same positions with only minor appearance changes.
outside_clip_unknowns: The identity of the object (food, mineral, biological tissue, etc.) and the medium around it.
Whether the surface swelling and the apparent droplet growth are part of a larger ongoing process that began before t=0 or continues after the last frame.
The cause of the gradual color/exposure shift (physical lighting change vs. camera/processing).
uncertain_details: Whether the growing amber feature is a true forming droplet or a change in reflection/wetting of an existing surface.
Whether the right-side bulge is physically expanding or only appears glossier due to the lighting shift.
Any very slight focus or exposure drift is hard to separate from genuine surface change given the dark background.

the excerpt form a complete story. Missing context outside this segment stays unknown.

do not invent a smooth transition or a causal mechanism to connect the two views.

properties. Cover the main visible process, not just scenery. Distinguish object movement from
camera movement, reflection from separate objects, expansion from translation, deformation from

and their relative positions before describing motion. Treat camera motion as uncertain when the
background evidence is insufficient, and retain clear relative changes despite that uncertainty.
